definitions.explanation: humble way to say that one will go along with someone of higher status

examples.japanese: ⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出張|しゅっちょう}→出張：01094_shucchou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お⟦{供|とも}→供：00462_tomo⟧します。
examples.english: I will accompany the president on his business trip.

examples.japanese: ぜひお⟦{供|とも}→供：00462_tomo⟧⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please allow me to accompany you.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お⟦{供|とも}→供：00462_tomo⟧した。
examples.english: I accompanied my teacher on her shopping.

notes:
KEIGO:
Humble speech (⟦{謙譲語|けんじょうご}→謙譲語：15869_kenjougo⟧): the speaker goes along with someone of higher status, such as a boss, client or teacher. Never used for what the other person does.
- お{供|とも}します: I will accompany you (polite)
- お{供|とも}⟦させて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦いただきます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧: I will accompany you (very humble)

RELATED WORDS:
- お{供|とも}: companion; attendant (noun)
- ⟦{同行|どうこう}する→同行する：21427_doukousuru⟧: to accompany — neutral, for business trips and official visits
- ⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go together — everyday, no humility

CULTURAL NOTE:
Historically, お{供|とも} were the servants or retainers who accompanied a lord. Today the verb is used in business and other formal situations.
